text.p: Pen pictures of the AC Milan players most likely to appear in Sunday's serie A clash with Juventus at the San Siro stadium:
SEBASTIANO ROSSI, goalkeeper, 32. First choice keeper since 1992 but fans blamed him for Milan's poor defensive record at start of this season. Unbeaten for record 929 minutes in serie A in 1994-95.

PAOLO MALDINI, defender, 28. Son of Italy coach Cesare, Maldini has been fixture in Milan since debut at age of 16 in 1985. Reputation as best-attacking full-back in world undermined by poor form for Italy at Euro 96 but scored a fabulous goal against Moldova at weekend. Italy captain.

FRANCO BARESI, defender, 36. Milan's longest-serving player in his 20th season with Milan. Symbol of club's transformation under Silvio Berlusconi, lifting three European Cups and five league titles in 10 years. Has kept everyone guessing about his retirement plans, on current form may not be imminent.

PIETRO VIERCHOWOD, 38 on Sunday. Oldest man in serie A, hoping to celebrate his birthday in action against his former team mates. Left Juventus at end of last season after playing in European Cup final. Joined Perugia but then walked out. Given new life at Milan. Scored against Roma this month.

MARCEL DESAILLY, defender, 28. With Marseille side that defeated Milan in 1993 European Cup final. At Milan six months later, where, at Baresi's request, filled holding role between midfield and defence. Nicknamed "The Rock", Desailly is now filling central defensive role he holds in French side.

DEMETRIO ALBERTINI, midfielder, 25. Reared in Milan youth team but farmed out to Padova for season before earning first-team place in 1991. Playmaker in Milan and national side. Packs powerful shot. Penalty-taker. First league goal versus Juventus in 1991. Committed Catholic whose brother is a priest.
ZVONIMIR BOBAN, midfielder, 28. Started with Dynamo Zagreb. Signed for Milan in 1991 but lent to Bari for season. Gifted passer and Croatia captain. Keen chess player.

STEFANO ERANIO, midfielder, 30. Started career with home-town Genoa, reaching 1992 UEFA Cup semi-finals before joining Milan. Aggressive midfielder with fierce shot. Italian international who missed 1994 World Cup because of injury.

DEJAN SAVICEVIC, midfielder, 30. Montenegrin signed from Red Star Belgrade in 1992. Fell out with coach Fabio Capello and only took first-team place after Berlusconi intervened. Nicknamed "The Genie" for ability to conjure up openings. Coming back after suspension.

CRISTOPHE DUGARRY, striker, 25. French international signed from Bordeaux after playing key role in Milan's humiliating 3-0 UEFA Cup exit to same club. Big and strong in traditional centre-forward mould. Back-up to Weah.

MARCO SIMONE, striker, 28. Complete centre-forward -- slick on turn with eye for opportunist goal -- but waited until this season to claim first-team place, at Roberto Baggio's expense. Has not scored since September 25.

ROBERTO BAGGIO, striker, 30. Despite limited appearances, last year pulled off rare feat of successive league titles with two teams: Juve and Milan. 24 goals in 44 internationals. One more league goal would bring him level in all-time lists with Juventus legend Roberto Bettega on 129.

GEORGE WEAH, striker, 30. Last year's World, European and African player of the year. Capable of turning defeat into victory with inspired moments of skill but not this Sunday due to international duties elsewhere with Liberia.
ALESSANDRO COSTACURTA, defender, 30. Suspended. In 1994, yellow cards cost him place in World and European Cup finals.
